title: Concord: Rethinking Distributed Coherence for Software Caches in Serverless Environments
problem: Serverless functions incur high latency from frequent global storage accesses; existing node-local caching schemes either restrict each data item to a single cache node (causing frequent remote reads) or allow multi-node replication but impose heavy coherence overhead, neither being optimal for serverless access patterns characterized by frequent reads, strong temporal locality, and few concurrent writers.
motivation: Global storage access is a dominant performance bottleneck in serverless computing, and serverless workloads' unique access patterns (read-heavy, temporally local, small data items, few concurrent nodes per application) are not well-served by existing single-node or naive multi-replica caching strategies.
method: Concord adapts the cache coherence approach from hardware processors—a system that keeps multiple copies of data synchronized across locations—for serverless computing. It allows data to be replicated across multiple nodes and serves reads from any nearby copy, cutting latency by avoiding slow central-storage accesses. A centralized directory tracks where each data's copies live and coordinates invalidation or update messages on writes to prevent stale reads. The protocol exploits serverless patterns (heavy reads, few concurrent writes) to reduce traffic, tolerates node failures and frequent instance churn (as functions start and stop), and enables transactional storage operations and transparent data-aware function placement.
key_novelty: A directory-based coherence protocol that adapts hardware cache coherence principles to serverless environments, enabling multi-node data replication with efficient invalidation and supporting transactional storage operations and transparent data-aware function placement.
contributions: Concord: distributed software cache coherence system for serverless with directory-based multi-replica protocol
Coherence protocol resilient to node failures and frequent coherence domain changes from serverless churn
Transactional storage accesses unlocked as a new capability in serverless environments
Transparent data-aware function placement; 2.4x execution speedup and 1.7x throughput improvement on 16-node cluster vs. state-of-the-art, using only 4.8% of application memory

metrics.speedup: 2.4x execution speedup, 1.7x throughput improvement vs. state-of-the-art serverless caching on 16-node cluster

baselines: State-of-the-art serverless caching schemes (single-node and multi-node approaches)
limitations: Evaluation is on a 16-node cluster; scalability to very large serverless clusters with thousands of nodes and high write rates is not fully characterized.
primary_theme: hardware-inspired software cache coherence for serverless computing
